The folklore troll-class is historically continuous with the eddic jotnar/thurses; saga usage often calls jotnar 'troll'. Aligned (functional/continuity) rather than equated, since the folklore class is distinct from the mythological jotnar collective.
The Norse mara (the spirit that 'rides' the sleeper) is the etymological and phenomenological root of the contemporary sleep-paralysis Old Hag tradition; modern functional cognate, so aligned_with.
The female form of the fylgja (kynfylgja) overlaps conceptually with the protective dis; both are personal/familial tutelary female spirits, per Simek and Lindow.
The disir as fate-bound female collective overlap with the norns in their fate-determining function; aligned (functional) per Lindow.
Disir overlap functionally with the valkyrjur as numinous female beings associated with death and protection; aligned per Simek/Lindow.
The disablot fertility/ancestral cult and the figure of Freyja as Vanadis link the disir to the Vanir sphere; tentative functional alignment.
Both landvaettir and dvergar are chthonic place-bound numina of the Norse landscape; tentative functional alignment of land/earth spirits.
The landvaettir, as tutelary spirits of land and fertility of place, sit in the same earth-numen sphere as the Germanic earth-goddess Nerthus; tentative thematic alignment.
The draugr (the unquiet, barrow-bound dead) stands as the negative counterpart to the honored battle-dead Einherjar received into Valhalla; thematic contrast in Norse conceptions of the dead.
